action: Financial institutions using the FSI assessment portal: expect delays to submissions, warn named staff about targeted phishing, and review what documents you uploaded to the portal.
exec: A breach of the financial sector's own security watchdog damages trust and has paused security-rating submissions for member institutions.
impact: The portal was taken offline for emergency maintenance, delaying security rating verifications.
plain: Hackers got into a portal run by the agency that guards South Korea's banks. About 650 records on financial-sector staff were exposed; no customer financial data was taken.
summary: The body that protects South Korea's financial sector said on November 11 that it detected unauthorized access two days earlier to a portal about 3,000 organisations use for security assessments. Roughly 650 records were exposed: about 200 administrative documents, 300 employee names and birth dates and 350 masked user entries. Korean media report the intruder registered an account posing as a financial regulator official.
title: South Korea's Financial Security Institute breached through its security assessment portal

validation.note: Institute statement reported by MLex and a second outlet citing Yonhap and Chosun.
